races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden

runners_data.name: Always Magic
runners_data.note: Finished eighth on debut at 7f on good ground, clearly a hold-up horse being asked to compress into midfield here; trainer Jack W Davison returns no winners in 14 days and 70 days between runs is a fitness query — going is fine but the trip is a sharp drop to 5f.

runners_data.name: Dhikola
runners_data.note: Two runs both resulting in unplaced efforts at 6f on good ground; a natural hold-up type who will find it difficult to get back to the rear in a 16-runner 5f dash and will likely be racing in mid-division rather than off the pace, which tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Eagle Eclipse
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant for J A Stack, going and style entirely unknown; Seamie Heffernan is a strong booking at this level and the stable has run six times in 14 days suggesting active current form, though no hints are available on how this horse will travel.

runners_data.name: Give Me Liberty
runners_data.note: Three runs at 6-7f, all mid-division finishes; has headgear flagged and the strong McCreery yard is 3/14 in 14 days — but a hold-up horse at 5f is at a structural disadvantage here, and being forced forward out of role further complicates its already modest form.

runners_data.name: Invincible Irish
runners_data.note: Showed a tendency to fade in the finish when beaten 11th on sole start at 5f on good; a natural hold-up horse squeezed into mid-division by the field's composition, and the fade flag combined with that debut run makes this a very hard pitch.

runners_data.name: Nando The Great
runners_data.note: Finished 19th of 19 on debut over 6f just five days ago — the quick return is notable and the form is stark; a hold-up horse by style who faded badly last time, and while the yard (Paul W Flynn) is light on recent form, nothing in the record encourages.

runners_data.name: Walk On Harry
runners_data.note: Placed third at 5f on good ground on debut then eighth at 6f; Henry De Bromhead is 4/34 in 14 days and the horse carries headgear (t) — crucially this is a hold-up type who has already shown ability specifically at this trip, making it better equipped than most to absorb a mid-division slot.

runners_data.name: Annie Tips
runners_data.note: Eighth on sole start at 6f on good; a hold-up type by style who is effectively being redistributed into mid-division, and the fade flag compounds the concern — trainer James Dowling has a thin recent record and nothing here screams a step forward.

runners_data.name: Arrowstock
runners_data.note: Three runs at 5-6f, placing 4th, 5th and 6th each time on good ground — consistent without winning; a prominent-style runner with Ben Coen aboard who is well-suited to tracking Southern Boulevard and represents the most straightforward threat from just off the pace.

runners_data.name: Best Love
runners_data.note: Has form figures of 0, U, 4 at 5-6f; the 4th at 5f on good is the relevant piece and the prominent style suits this race shape — Jamie Powell rides and the Harty yard is quiet at present, but this is one of the better-profile prominent types in the field.

runners_data.name: Better Yet
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant for Mrs John Harrington with Shane Foley — that jockey-trainer combination commands respect; going and style are entirely unknown, but the booking alone elevates this above a typical debutant in a wide-open maiden.

runners_data.name: My Irish Lady
runners_data.note: Finished 10th and 6th at 5f on good ground for J P Murtagh; a hold-up type whose best effort (6th) came at this exact trip and going, and with Rory Mulligan (5) claiming, there may be a slight weight relief angle though the form is unspectacular.

runners_data.name: Ocean Surge
runners_data.note: Eighth on debut at 6f 61 days ago with a fade flag; a hold-up horse returning after a break for McCreery, who is in form (3/14), but one run and a fade tendency makes this a significant unknown stepping back in trip.

runners_data.name: Southern Boulevard
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner, ridden by Colin Keane for G M Lyons — form of 3rd and 5th at 5f on good is exactly relevant, and the uncontested lead on a flat 5f course with no pace rival is a significant tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Stormy Dawn
runners_data.note: Finished 12th on debut at 7f on good 36 days ago with a fade flag; a hold-up type dropping sharply in trip — the combination of a poor debut, a fading tendency, a trip reduction and an apprentice booking (Keithen Kennedy, 5) gives little reason for optimism.

runners_data.name: Syrah
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant for Charles Weld ridden by apprentice Patrick McGettigan (5); Weld's yard has been quiet (0/2 in 14 days) and the apprentice booking is less exciting than some rivals — style and going entirely unknown, so this is genuinely a blank slate.

races.paceDynamic: Southern Boulevard is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with Colin Keane aboard for G M Lyons, will stride straight to the lead from the off in this 5f maiden — entirely uncontested, able to dictate every fraction on good ground. The pace is unlikely to be suicidal; Southern Boulevard will control tempo from the front rail and force every rival to chase rather than hunt down a pace-pressed leader. With no genuine second front-runner to threaten the lead, the pace shape is moderate-to-sustainable, which historically on Cork's flat 5f track rewards horses racing prominently and finishing the race out rather than sweeping from deep. The race shape therefore firmly favours prominent or close-tracking runners who can latch onto the leader's back early and match strides into the final furlong; pure hold-up horses face a significant disadvantage as there is no pace collapse to exploit. The field contains substantially more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Invincible Irish, Give Me Liberty, Dhikola and Annie Tips are all genuine hold-up horses who are likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield rather than their preferred position, and of those, Give Me Liberty and Dhikola are probably best placed to adjust given their experience.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Southern Boulevard Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Southern Boulevard is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a measured, sustainable gallop that suits those just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Southern Boulevard dictates every fraction and the race becomes a procession from the front, with prominent-ridden horses like Arrowstock and Best Love the only threats as they track close and are poised to challenge approaching the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Reel In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Arrowstock or Best Love press Southern Boulevard harder than expected and turn it into a genuine speed duel down the straight.
scenarios.body: The injection of pressure from one or both prominent types compresses the finishing order, and a fresh hold-up horse — Walk On Harry, who showed ability to finish at 5f — picks up the pieces as the pace-makers tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three unraced runners — Better Yet, Eagle Eclipse, or Syrah — is significantly ahead of a low starting line and debuts with a performance that renders experience irrelevant.
scenarios.body: A high-class newcomer trained by a yard capable of landing a debut win (Better Yet with Shane Foley for Mrs John Harrington being the most plausible given jockey booking) breaks smartly and travels prominently to outstay the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Peg Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and all the redistributed hold-up horses are caught flat-footed by a dawdling early tempo that plays directly into Southern Boulevard's hands.
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace collapse, horses like Dhikola, Invincible Irish, Annie Tips and Give Me Liberty — all racing out of their natural hold-up role and mapped mid-field — find themselves with no ground to make up, and the front end dominates throughout.

watchPoints.text: Southern Boulevard (Colin Keane / G M Lyons) goes unchallenged to the lead — if no rival moves to press in the first furlong, watch for the race to effectively be over by halfway as the lone pace-setter controls every fraction.

Arrowstock and Best Love are the only prominent-style experienced horses capable of bridging the gap to Southern Boulevard — if either is slow out of the stalls or loses a length at the break, their ability to land a prominent position may be compromised in a 16-runner field.

Better Yet (Shane Foley / Mrs John Harrington) is a debutant with a high-quality booking; watch the market move closely as a strongly-supported newcomer arriving fresh and professionally prepared can outclass a maiden field regardless of race shape.

Multiple hold-up horses — Dhikola, Invincible Irish, Give Me Liberty, Annie Tips and Always Magic — are all likely to race closer to the pace than natural, creating potential for mid-race bunching and interference on what is a straight 5f course with a large field.

Walk On Harry (Henry De Bromhead) carries headgear for the first time and has the sole piece of solid placed form at exactly 5f on good ground in this field — monitor how it travels in the early stages as it is the most interesting hold-up type that may genuinely see out the trip.

races.name: OCS Recruitment Handicap

runners_data.name: Kiss Don't Tell
runners_data.note: Prominent racer trained by Daniel McLoughlin, returning from 254 days off which is a significant fitness query; has placed on similar going (2nd at 5f/STA) and should secure a forward position just off the two front-runners, making her a key pace-map beneficiary if fitness is there.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up effort last time out makes Kiss Don't Tell a genuine threat here, and she has run over today's trip and going before; the main concern is 254 days off the track, which leaves her fitness on trust.

runners_data.name: Amerilis
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with five recent runs in form, including two placings at 5-6f on good ground and a solid record of 5 runs on similar going with consistent finishes; wears a hood and tongue-tie, and Donagh O'Connor's booking is an upgrade — her best chance is if the pace flattens slightly.
runners_data.comment: Amerilis shaped with plenty of promise when runner-up last time out and again three starts back, and she holds strong claims as the top-rated runner in the field; winless in her last five starts, but her rating of 73 suggests she is on a mark she can exploit.

runners_data.name: Gonna Be Golden
runners_data.note: True hold-up type whose best recent effort was a 3rd on soft ground over 5f; trainer A. Oliver in solid recent form (3/11 in 14 days) but this horse's good-ground record is poor (3 efforts, no wins or places) and Sam Coen claims 5lbs, which helps the weight but cannot mask the style mismatch in a pace-pressured race.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of twelve on our ratings, Gonna Be Golden brings experience of today's trip and going and last ran 27 days ago, but she remains winless in her last six starts and that inconsistency is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: The Right One
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner with four placed efforts and a win on soft at 5f; good-ground record of 8 runs shows consistency but just 0 wins and 4 places — will need to assert over Cashel Blue from the gates, and Ronan Whelan is a strong booking to manage the pace contest tactically.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win two starts back before a below-par latest effort, and The Right One has experience of today's distance and going in her favour; the main concern is reproducing that winning form after an unplaced return.

runners_data.name: Cashel Blue
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter with a C&D win on good ground and a recent 3rd at 5f/GOO; W.J. Lee takes over in the saddle for K.J. Condon, and this horse's 1 win from 5 runs on similar going is solid evidence of genuine ability at this course and trip — the draw and early position battle with The Right One is the pivotal tactical factor.
runners_data.comment: Cashel Blue showed she can find the frame, winning two starts back and third last time out, though she was out of the money in between; she has run over today's trip and going, but 137 lb from stall 12 gives her plenty to shoulder.

runners_data.name: Lilbittyprettyone
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with limited good-ground exposure (1 run, 0 wins/places) who has shown her better efforts on soft; Rebecca Parsons claims 10lbs but the style means she needs the pace to collapse, which is unlikely given the front-runner battle, and the amateur's claim offers modest compensation.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Lilbittyprettyone at least has experience of today's trip and going to call on, and 33 days between runs suggests she returns fresh; the 134 lb burden from stall seven, however, makes progress hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Smart Sioux
runners_data.note: Flagged as a fader in the finish, returning from 125 days off for a modest yard; good-ground record shows she struggles to sustain effort over 5f on this surface, and with no wins or places in 4 eligible runs, the layoff and finishing pattern make her hard to support in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and 125 days absent, Smart Sioux faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 63 gives her a shade of untapped potential to work with.

runners_data.name: Sceitimini
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan is a powerful booking for this modest yard, and the horse has shown occasional ability to place in good-ground sprints; however, her true running style is a deep hold-up, and the crowded rear of this field means she will not get her natural position — the style-fit score of 0.92 reflects a real risk of racing uncomfortably wide or boxed in midfield.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Sceitimini is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 42-day break with a fresh chance to reverse a run of disappointing efforts.

runners_data.name: Simmering Seas
runners_data.note: Returning from 125 days off with a pattern of finishing mid-pack on good ground (four runs, no wins or places on similar going); genuinely wants to come from off the pace, but in this race configuration she is unlikely to get to the rear of the field where she operates best, blunting her effectiveness considerably.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after 125 days off, Simmering Seas faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 61 suggests some residual ability that her recent finishes have not reflected.

runners_data.name: Another Nice'day
runners_data.note: Has a win and a place to her name and is lightly weighted on OR=52, but her preferred closing style is compromised here — despite being a genuine hold-up type, she is squeezed into a midfield slot by the sheer volume of similar runners; recent form shows good-ground placings but also a string of mid-teens finishes on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Beaten into seventh last time out and well below his one recent win two starts back, Another Nice'day ranks bottom of this field on our figures and looks hard to fancy at a mark of 52, though he has run over today's trip and going and a light weight of 124 lb from stall one offers marginal compensation.

runners_data.name: Lady Landhort
runners_data.note: Nathan Crosse takes over for the McLoughlin yard; her best effort is a win on Flat/STA conditions rather than good ground, and 4 runs on similar going have produced no wins or placed efforts — mapped to midfield from her natural hold-up base, she would need a significant underperformance by the front half of the field to get involved.

runners_data.name: Love Bomb
runners_data.note: Wears a visor for W. McCreery, who is in strong form (3/14 in 14 days), but this filly's good-ground record spans 9 runs with just 1 win and 1 place — her fade pattern and deep hold-up style mean the redistribution to midfield is an uncomfortable fit, and in a genuinely-run sprint she is unlikely to reach the placed positions.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a string of mid-field and unplaced efforts making her hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a reasonable 21-day break.

races.paceDynamic: The Right One and Cashel Blue are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the gates in this 5f handicap on good ground at Cork, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a soft, uncontested lead for either. With both horses needing to be prominent to be effective — The Right One has four placed efforts from prominent/lead position in similar going, and Cashel Blue won over C&D on good — the pace will be honest from the outset, which compresses the advantage of leading and stretches the race into a genuine test of stamina for five furlongs. Kiss Don't Tell is the only other natural prominent racer likely to secure a forward position close to the speed, while the remainder of the field is overwhelmingly hold-up in profile. This race shape — contested pace over a flat 5f on good ground — most directly favours horses that can race prominently just off the two front-runners, absorb a genuine gallop, and sustain their effort through the final furlong, tilting the advantage toward the prominent profile and penalising true closers who will find limited late cut in the ground. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can genuinely accommodate at the rear: Sceitimini, Simmering Seas, Another Nice'day, Lady Landhort, and Love Bomb are all redistributed from their natural back-of-field position into midfield slots, with Sceitimini and Lady Landhort most likely to actually get closest to that role given their class and recency.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Hold Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If The Right One and Cashel Blue fight for the lead and the runner-up spot settles into a solid rhythm that suits the horse closest to but just off the pace.
scenarios.body: The honest early gallop set by two genuine front-runners burns the leaders out approaching the final furlong, handing advantage to whichever horse has tracked within two lengths and maintained cover throughout; good ground favours sustained galloping over late finishing bursts on this flat 5f track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Fight Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters buries the other in the first two furlongs and opens up an unassailable lead by halfway.
scenarios.body: Either The Right One or Cashel Blue, having seen off their principal rival for the front position, dictates a controlled gallop and uses the flat straight to grind home; The Right One's recent winning form at this trip and going makes this credible, while Cashel Blue's C&D win shows the course suits.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners cancel each other out prematurely and the tempo unexpectedly flattens over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A collapse in pace in the latter stages allows the best-positioned midfield horse to pick up the pieces without needing a true late burst; Amerilis has shown ability to finish from off the pace on similar going with multiple placed efforts at 5-6f, making her the likeliest beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly searching and burns every placed horse, opening the door for horses at the rear to finish through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends heavily on redistributed hold-up types — Sceitimini, Simmering Seas, and Another Nice'day — getting to actually race from their natural position, which is unlikely given the congested rear of the field; the style-fit discounts across these runners mean this is the least reliable shape and would require an unusually severe early burn-up.

watchPoints.text: The Right One vs Cashel Blue: watch whether either horse breaks markedly faster from the gates — if one buries the other in the first furlong and opens a clear lead, the race outcome changes sharply from a contested scenario to a front-runner dictating on her own terms.

Kiss Don't Tell is returning from 254 days off and has not been seen since last season; if she shows any sign of greenness or ring-rustiness in the early furlongs, she loses her principal asset as the horse best-placed to track the pace from a prominent angle.

Cashel Blue's jockey change to W.J. Lee warrants monitoring in the betting market — if the market firms significantly for Cashel Blue, it may indicate stable confidence that Lee can out-manoeuvre The Right One for the front position and control the tempo.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Sceitimini, Simmering Seas, Another Nice'day, Lady Landhort, Love Bomb) will create genuine traffic and positional congestion from the 3f pole inward — watch for any of these runners getting boxed in or forced wider than ideal on the straight track.

Amerilis's hood and tongue-tie combination is worth noting if she settles better than usual in the early stages; any improvement in her jumping-off position relative to her natural hold-up role could make her a more dangerous factor in Scenario C than her redistribution tag implies.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Firville Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Alpine Wedding
runners_data.note: Runner-up on debut over 7f on good ground gives her the right profile for this trip and surface, and Paul Twomey's yard is in reasonable form (2/8 last 14 days); she races naturally prominent and should be able to hold that position comfortably given she is not one of the redistributed types, though the step up in class from that debut placing is significant.
runners_data.comment: Alpine Wedding showed a placed effort last time out and has run over today's trip, but she carries 128 lb from stall ten and her speed rating of 59 gives pause — third last time out offers encouragement, yet she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Alwaysanangel
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground most recently and Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over for Joseph O'Brien — a powerful combination at this level; a genuine hold-up performer who will be produced late, she is ideally suited to the honest pace the two front-runners should set, though the step from 6f to 7f is untested.
runners_data.comment: Alwaysanangel arrives in fine nick after a win two starts back, has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 86 heads the field; the one query is whether 35 days off has left her short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Beibhinn
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's filly has winning form on good ground and hit the frame in three of her four starts, but her natural instinct is to race prominently and, given the congestion at the front of this field, she will likely find herself pushed back against her preferred style — that positional squeeze rather than her ability is the key uncertainty here.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in her last two starts and a winner three starts back, Beibhinn arrives fresh on 26 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going and a handy draw in stall three lending her good claims here.

runners_data.name: Celtic Moon
runners_data.note: John Murtagh sends this filly in fresh off a 15-day turnaround and her only win came over 8f on good ground; she naturally wants to race close to the pace but the crowded early positions in this race mean she is unlikely to secure that berth, and running against her natural style on a step back in trip makes her a difficult proposition.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out blunts her claims, though she did score two starts back and her experience over today's trip and going suggests conditions hold no fears; the 128 lb burden from stall 2 is the other factor to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Damsel In Distress
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good ground for Daniel McLoughlin and steps back to 7f here; she races prominently and the slightly shorter trip may suit her pace, though the trainer is 0/7 in the last 14 days and a 45-day absence adds a small question mark despite her clean record on this going.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Damsel In Distress makes it hard to build a case, though she does bring a win last time out and experience of today's trip and going to the table.

runners_data.name: Film Set
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's debutante, who ran a single unplaced effort over 6f on good ground, represents the stable's hold-up card in a race where they also control the pace through Nevermindtherain and Madam Secretary; Ronan Whelan has the riding brief and the step to 7f should unlock more of her stamina, though she remains lightly exposed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and ranked last on our figures, Film Set faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a trainer firing at 26% in the last 14 days offers some hope.

runners_data.name: Madam Secretary
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes over for Aidan O'Brien and she has placed in all three starts on good and similar ground; she is one of the two confirmed front-runners in this field and Moore's involvement suggests she will be ridden to lead rather than restrained, making her the pace-setting horse most likely to dictate terms if she can assert over Nevermindtherain early.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in her last three starts — placed third two starts back and again three starts back, and second last time out — Madam Secretary has distance and going experience in her favour, and a trainer firing at 26% adds encouragement, though her rating of 78 gives her something to find on the figures.

runners_data.name: Maeda Matsu
runners_data.note: Ran second over 6f on good ground on her only start for Sheila Lavery and Robbie Colgan takes the ride here; she races prominently and will need to find improvement at Listed level on a step up to 7f, with limited evidence to assess whether the extra furlong suits.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Maeda Matsu faces a stiff task, though she returns on a quick turnaround of 11 days off a runner-up finish last time and has experience of today's going in her favour.

runners_data.name: Maire Rua
runners_data.note: Colin Keane picks up the ride for Ger Lyons on a filly who won over 7f on good ground on debut — the ideal profile for this race on paper; she is a natural prominent racer who should slot in without needing to fight for position, and the combination of course-relevant winning form and a top jockey makes her one of the more straightforward profiles in the field.
runners_data.comment: Maire Rua arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, giving her a solid platform to follow up; the concern is whether 36 days off has left her short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Nevermindtherain
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's filly has four starts on the board, all on good ground, and has placed twice over 7f — this trip is her best distance; she is one of the two confirmed pace-setters but has yet to win and her form shows consistency rather than dominance, meaning she may find the pace duel with Madam Secretary draining rather than releasing.
runners_data.comment: Consistent place-getter who has finished third in each of her last two starts, though she remains yet to win in recent starts and a speed rating of 80 suggests she may just lack the necessary finishing kick; the trainer's 26% strike rate over the last 14 days offers encouragement.

runners_data.name: Shi Yang
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground most recently for Robson De Aguiar, which gives her winning form at the right trip and going, but she fundamentally wants to be prominent and the crowded pace positions in this race mean she cannot fulfil that role — operating out of her preferred position is likely to blunt the finishing effort that delivered her win.
runners_data.comment: Shi Yang arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, giving her a solid each-way profile at 128 lb from stall nine; the slight dip in form two starts back is the one note of caution.

races.paceDynamic: Nevermindtherain and Madam Secretary are the two confirmed front-runners in this 11-runner Listed contest, and with both handlers (Aidan O'Brien has both) likely to let them stride, the early pace will be genuine and contested rather than manufactured. Nevermindtherain has shown a tendency to race prominently across all her starts and Madam Secretary brings Ryan Moore aboard — that combination means the pace will be set honestly from the gates, creating a true-run 7f on good ground at Cork. The result should be a race that stretches the field through the middle sections, placing maximum emphasis on runners who can settle off the pace and sustain their effort into the straight rather than those who burn energy fighting for early position. This shape heavily favours hold-up and genuine mid-division closers who can find clear running in the straight — Alwaysanangel and Film Set are the natural beneficiaries — while Alpine Wedding, Damsel In Distress and Maire Rua must deliver from prominent ground without getting caught in the early contest. The field holds more prominent-minded types than can all secure their natural position: of the redistributed trio, Beibhinn has the class and recent form to be most likely to push up and actually hold a forward berth, with Celtic Moon and Shi Yang more likely to find themselves squeezed back against their natural style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Genuine pace, closers finish
scenarios.trigger: If Nevermindtherain and Madam Secretary fight for the early lead and ensure a true gallop that strings the field out.
scenarios.body: The sustained honest pace burns off those who over-race and sets up the straight perfectly for runners arriving with momentum; hold-up horses who have been produced with a clean run will have the most energy in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace duel collapses, prominent wins
scenarios.trigger: If the front two do not fully test each other and a prominent racer just off the lead inherits a slender advantage turning for home.
scenarios.body: A pace that looks genuine early but does not truly stretch the field leaves those racing in second or third with a decisive positional advantage; a prominent horse with a good cruising speed can exploit the gap left when the leaders fade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner survives contested pace
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two confirmed front-runners — most likely Madam Secretary with Ryan Moore — asserts early dominance and the rival capitulates.
scenarios.body: Moore's tactical intelligence could allow Madam Secretary to find a controlling rhythm once Nevermindtherain is put under pressure and drops away; a front-runner who owns the pace rather than fights for it can recycle energy and hold on in a truly run race on good ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field bunches, sprint finish
scenarios.trigger: If the two pace horses cancel each other out very early and the field concertinas, turning a 7f race into a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: With the pace collapsing, position and raw speed over the final two furlongs matter most; horses with a high top-speed figure and a sharp turn of foot can win a sprint finish even from off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Madam Secretary and Nevermindtherain are on a collision course for the early lead — watch whether Moore asserts immediately at the gates or allows Nevermindtherain to take the role, because whichever horse is forced to fight hardest in the first two furlongs is the one most likely to capitulate turning for home.

Beibhinn, Celtic Moon and Shi Yang are all natural prominent racers who will be squeezed for early position — if any of the three are seen bustling for room in the first furlong, they are unlikely to recover their rhythm and their chance should be marked down significantly in running.

Alwaysanangel is the most natural hold-up horse in the field but her single win came over 6f — watch how Dylan Browne McMonagle positions her in the early stages, because if he is forced to make ground too early to compensate for the 7f trip, she may not see it out in the way the pace scenario suggests she should.

Maire Rua's debut win came over this exact trip on good ground and Colin Keane is one of the strongest jockeys in the field — watch whether Keane is able to slot her into a prominent position without expending energy in the early pace contest, because a clean run in second or third would make her the ideal positional beneficiary if the pace collapses slightly.

races.paceDynamic: Spinning Around is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse committed to leading, she should be able to dictate an honest but uncontested gallop on good ground over seven furlongs at Cork. The prominent group is congested — Carolina Jetstream, Treasure Rose, L L Koulsty, Sindagan, and Suzie Songs all want to race close to the pace, meaning there will be genuine scrapping for the best rail positions in the first two furlongs and a real risk of traffic interference between two and three out as that cluster compresses. Fort Vega, Keke, Princess Child, and Tahcawin are the natural hold-up horses, and they should have clear daylight behind the prominent pack to deliver their finishing runs. This field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the field can naturally accommodate — Nancy J and Temperance are genuine closers who are likely to be shuffled into midfield rather than tracking from their preferred deep position, which tempers their chance materially. A genuine gallop with a well-positioned prominent horse tracking the leader and quickening in the straight is the dominant outcome, strongly favouring horses that race in the P-to-M band and can travel into the race rather than launching from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Spinning Around sets a true honest gallop and the prominent pack settles just behind, allowing a clean-travelling prominent horse to kick at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Spinning Around lays down a consistent fractions-based lead on good ground, and the horses sitting second or third have the perfect slingshot as the field fans wide in the straight; the seven-furlong trip suits a horse that can sustain a run from three out rather than sprint over five.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group pushes the early pace harder than expected while fighting for position, tying itself up and leaving late runners with a clear passage.
scenarios.body: The scrapping among Carolina Jetstream, Treasure Rose, L L Koulsty, and Suzie Songs quickens the opening fractions and the field strings out, creating a gap for the true hold-up horses to thread through off a genuine tempo; Fort Vega, who has run multiple good 7f races on good ground in this exact form, is the horse best placed to exploit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Lasts
scenarios.trigger: If Spinning Around, completely uncontested in front, dictates a conservative early pace that allows her to coast through the middle portions and still have enough in reserve entering the straight.
scenarios.body: On good ground at Cork she can control every yard of the race unchallenged, and any wire-to-wire verdict would require the trailing horses to fail to close a gap they never truly set up; her trainer Donnacha Aidan O'Brien and jockey Gavin Ryan will know this shape and could exploit it deliberately.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Congestion Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent traffic battle becomes chaotic between two and three furlongs out, creating interference that eliminates the fancied closers and promotes whichever horse finds an unexpected clean route.
scenarios.body: A scrambled mid-race produces an untidy home straight where position and luck matter as much as ability; a horse sitting just off the pace but unaffected by the scrimmage benefits most, while the redistribted hold-up horses who are racing out of their natural role are least likely to profit from this messy shape.

watchPoints.text: Prominent traffic between furlongs 5 and 4 — Carolina Jetstream, Treasure Rose, L L Koulsty, Sindagan, and Suzie Songs are all vying for the same two or three positions behind Spinning Around, and a bump or squeeze in that cluster could eliminate multiple fancied horses at a critical point.

Nancy J and Temperance are genuine hold-up horses who will likely be denied their natural ground-saving positions and forced to race in midfield — watch whether either can find a clear passage despite racing out of role, as it will directly shape their finishing effort.

Spinning Around's pace control is central to the race shape — if Gavin Ryan allows the pace to drop in the middle section, the holds-ups will be denied the tempo they need to reel in the leader, and the wire-to-wire scenario becomes suddenly more live.

L L Koulsty is the only runner with a recent winning run at this exact course and distance on good ground — monitor his draw and early position in running, as his map puts him ideally placed to shadow the leader without burning petrol.

Princess Child's 82-day absence is the longest layoff in the field — watch her in the parade ring for condition, as Dylan Browne McMonagle is a significant booking but fresh returns for hold-up types over 7f at Cork on good ground require scrutiny.

races.paceDynamic: Caught U Sleeping is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Colin Keane aboard, will stride comfortably to the front from the outset, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop on good ground over 1m4f at Cork. Behind her, a congested prominent group — Bosphorus Rose, Nyra, Amelia Earhart, and Cameo — will jostle for the best seats in the first three furlongs, creating genuine traffic risk between the 3f and 2f markers as they stack up behind the leader. Snapretend and Believed are natural prominent types who will find that position already taken and will be forced to race in a more restrained midfield than suits them, effectively compromising their optimal race shape. With one unhurried pace-setter and a bunched chasing group unable to apply early pressure, this setup overwhelmingly favours hold-up horses with a strong late run — specifically those with the class and finishing kick to pick through a compacting field in the straight — and the two genuine hold-up types, Ankara and Ice Dancer, are the stylistic beneficiaries, though Ankara's tendency to fade in the finish is a meaningful caveat.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Caught U Sleeping controls unchallenged

scenarios.body: Keane sets fractions that are fast enough to be honest but slow enough to leave petrol in the tank, and the prominent runners exhaust themselves jostling for position rather than pressing the leader; Caught U Sleeping kicks clear inside the final 2f before they can organise a challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent surge 2f out

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late closers pounce

scenarios.body: Both are racing out of their natural role and their style-fit discount (0.94 and 0.90) reflects genuine compromise, but a chaotic straight could open gaps that negate the positional disadvantage; Believed's recent form string of 42133 is the strongest argument for her in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Caught U Sleeping's ability to get a completely uncontested lead is the single biggest tactical factor — watch if any prominent runner (particularly Bosphorus Rose or Amelia Earhart) attempts to press her early, as it would fundamentally change the pace equation.

The cluster of Bosphorus Rose, Nyra, Amelia Earhart, and Cameo will create dangerous traffic between the 3f and 2f markers — any horse on the inner of that group risks being blocked or checked at the critical moment.

Snapretend's 83-day absence combined with racing out of her natural prominent role makes her a significant risk factor — she could either bounce back with a bold display or be completely lost for room from an unnatural position.

Nyra's jockey booking — Dylan Browne McMonagle — is notable given the Joseph O'Brien stable also runs Snapretend with Scott McCullagh; the senior booking arguably signals where the yard's main hope lies between their two runners.

Ice Dancer has worn a hood (hg:b) and her string of very poor finishes on good ground suggests the step to 1m4f in this company has not sparked a revival — monitor in the paddock for any signs of cause for optimism before treating her as a live factor.

races.paceDynamic: Garden Party is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Ryan Moore aboard for the powerful A P O'Brien yard, she is virtually certain to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo over this 1m2½f trip on Good ground at Cork. Saxony Charms (Colin Keane) is the only confirmed prominent runner and will likely track Garden Party through the first half of the race, with the remainder of the field — dominated by hold-up types — settling in behind. With one pace-setter and one genuine stalker, this sets up as a slowly-run-to-the-straight affair before a prolonged gallop from the home turn, favouring horses with a mid-race kick rather than deep closers who need a true end-to-end test. The field holds more hold-up types than can all find their natural position at the rear; Elusive In Mayo, Serendipia, and Chosen One are redistributed to midfield on the map but in reality the division between midfield and hold-up will be compressed, and Zadawa — a genuine hold-up horse with Good-ground course form — is best placed to exploit any late injection of pace. The race shape strongly favours the prominent profile: Saxony Charms sits in an ideal position to attack the leader in the straight, and any horse with a clean turn of foot from a handy pitch will be at a significant advantage over deep closers with nowhere to make up ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Garden Party Controls, Saxony Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Party sets a measured tempo and Saxony Charms tracks throughout before challenging decisively in the straight.
scenarios.body: Garden Party's lone lead creates a falsely steady pace that rewards the horse best positioned to pounce at the two-furlong pole; Saxony Charms has already shown a finishing position of third and fifth over this type of Good ground at 10f and is ideally placed to strike. Moore's tactical awareness means the pace will be metronomic rather than dawdling, giving Saxony Charms and any prominent tracker the perfect platform.

scenarios.body: With the race run at an honest but not brutal tempo, a talented debutante from a top stable can cruise into contention without being harmed by the pace dynamics and produce a sustained finishing run on Good ground that the experienced hold-up horses simply cannot match. Fairylike (A P O'Brien, Wayne Lordan) holds the most obvious profile here given trainer form figures of 9/34 over 14 days — raw ability could paper over any inexperience.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Cavalry Arrives Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough in the final quarter-mile for deep closers to pick off tiring leaders from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: This shape requires Garden Party to set a faster-than-expected tempo that strings the field out and leaves the front two exhausted by the entrance to the straight; Zadawa (D K Weld, Chris Hayes) has genuine hold-up credentials, Good-ground form at 10f, and a trainer who excels with fillies stepping up in distance, making her the prime beneficiary if the pace collapses ahead. Chosen One and Serendipia are mapped to midfield but are true hold-up types — their STYLE_FIT discount means this scenario's probability is suppressed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Carnage — Wide-Open Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is muddled through the middle stages, causing bunching and a chaotic sprint finish where positional luck dominates.
scenarios.body: A compressed field emerging from Cork's final bend in a heap benefits horses with the widest draw, sharpest reaction, and cleanest passage — Emily Estherfaye and Trumph have soft-ground experience at 12f suggesting they stay further than today's field and could grind through a messy finish. This is the least structured outcome and requires multiple pace miscalculations from experienced jockeys, making it the lowest-probability shape.

watchPoints.text: Garden Party sets the only confirmed pace — if Ryan Moore rolls along at a crawl in the early stages, the entire race becomes a sprint for the final two furlongs and horses further back than Saxony Charms will find it nearly impossible to reach the winner.

Salamina ran just two days ago and, despite Dylan Browne McMonagle in the saddle, a horse with a fade-in-finish flag and such a quick turnaround could drop away sharply after halfway — watch whether she weakens early, which would confirm a strong pace and open up the race for closers.

Fairylike and The Blonde Lady are both unraced with going marked UNKNOWN — if either breaks sharply and establishes an early prominent position, the race map changes significantly, as Garden Party would face unexpected company and could be pressured into going faster than intended.

Elusive In Mayo carries the joint-highest OR in the field at 120 but has only one run (12th of 12) and a noted fade pattern — if she suddenly challenges Garden Party for the early lead, watch for the pace to dramatically increase and unsettle the comfortable lead scenario that currently dominates the probabilities.

Serendipia, Chosen One, and Elusive In Mayo are all genuinely hold-up horses compressed into a midfield slot — watch how W J Lee, Paddy Harnett, and Nicola Burns handle the first two furlongs, as any crowding or interference in the early-mid section could compromise all three simultaneously and distort the race shape.

runners_data.name: Launch Time
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with Colin Keane aboard — recent win over 8f on good ground is directly relevant, and the absence of genuine pace rivals makes her task structurally straightforward; tagged STYLE_FIT for a prominent role she rarely needs to force, but here she simply leads naturally.
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out and third two starts back, Launch Time arrives in good recent nick after just eight days, though that ninth three starts back hints at inconsistency; he has run over today's trip and going, but 140 lb from stall 14 is no easy ask.

runners_data.name: Sheamus Seimhiu
runners_data.note: Returns after a 291-day absence for Chris Timmons, who has a 0/2 recent record, and has shown a persistent pattern of fading in the finish on similar going — the layoff and weak trainer form combine to make this a very difficult winning profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 291 days off, Sheamus Seimhiu does at least have experience of today's trip and conditions and a rating of 60 suggests he retains ability, though his inconsistent recent form is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Half Cut
runners_data.note: Tony Phelan's charge arrives on tongue-tie with a fade flag and a poor recent run at longer trips; the drop back to a flat mile on good going is a mild positive but the finishing tendency is a concern, and the trainer has been cold recently.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked near the foot of our assessments, Half Cut faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's going before, and 25 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but the handicapper's mark of 55 looks beyond him on recent evidence.

runners_data.name: James Henry
runners_data.note: A genuinely strong hold-up performer by nature — seven-year-old with three placed efforts in recent good-ground miles — but the field density means he is very unlikely to slot into his preferred position off the pace; Chris Hayes rides and the recent form shows competitive efforts without a win.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, James Henry showed his quality with back-to-back thirds three and four starts back, and his experience over today's trip and conditions gives him a clear edge; the concern is his two unplaced efforts since, which he must reverse from stall 19 carrying 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Glamazon
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the ride for Mrs Harrington who is active in the book; the filly's one win came at 10f on good ground and she has placed several times at 8f, making the trip and conditions a legitimate fit — her hold-up style is genuine but she races prominently enough to avoid the redistribution squeeze.
runners_data.comment: Glamazon has run over today's trip and going, and a win five starts back gives her something to build on, though her last three outings have been below par; from draw 11 off 136 lb, the top-rated runner here still has the profile to go well fresh at 30 days.

runners_data.name: Imnotleavinyou
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce (3lb claim) partners this three-year-old who won over 7f on good ground earlier in the season; the horse handles the surface well based on her record (11/15 on similar going) and has placed twice at this type of level, giving her solid claims in a shape that suits a finisher.
runners_data.comment: Imnotleavinyou won five starts back and has experience of today's distance and going, arriving here on a fresher 18-day turnaround with conditions to suit; the risk is that her recent form has been patchy, with three fifth-place finishes and an unplaced run since that victory.

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over for Paul Flynn — three of her last five starts produced top-3 finishes on good ground, all at 6-7f, so the step to a flat mile is worth monitoring; her hold-up tendency is genuine but she races close enough to the pace to avoid being buried by the redistribution problem.
runners_data.comment: Dawn Flame has shown a degree of consistency with thirds last time and three starts back, but he's yet to win in his last six outings and his trainer is in a barren run of form; his experience over today's trip and going offers some grounding, though the yard's current record gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Mountain Memory
runners_data.note: Trainer-jockey combination of Andrew Slattery is unusual; the three-year-old has only one run on good ground in this dataset and carries the fade flag — modest profile with little to recommend on current evidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Mountain Memory at least returns with a 33-day break and has run over today's trip, giving connections something to work with, though a rating of 55 and recent unplaced efforts suggest he faces a stiff task from stall ten carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Thompson Gunner
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by profile who won at 10f on standard ground earlier; only ran two days ago which is an immediate red flag, and in this field he is pushed into a midfield representation far removed from his natural rear-of-field position — the STYLE_FIT tag and short turnaround significantly temper his claims.
runners_data.comment: Thompson Gunner returns just two days after finishing third last time out, so fitness is not in doubt, but the quick turnaround and a hefty 134 lb to carry are stiff asks; he has run over today's trip and going before, and that sole recent win four starts back adds hope for a competitive midfield runner rated 60.

runners_data.name: Morning Approach
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran for Willie McCreery, running off OR 48 with a fade tendency and a history of finishing 11th-14th in similar company — his true hold-up style is compromised by being mapped closer than he would naturally race, and recent form offers very little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Morning Approach arrives on the back of an unplaced effort twenty days ago and faces a stiff task from stall 15 carrying 131 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 55 offers modest encouragement.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: The most likely companion to Launch Time up front for Michael Mulvany; terry Casey (7lb claim) rides and the form shows a second-place finish over 10f on good ground six runs back — if she is competitive, she benefits from the position rather than a pronounced turn of foot.
runners_data.comment: Borora Aura returns quickly on nine days' rest and has run over today's trip and going, but she is winless in her last six starts and her second three starts back reads as a lone bright spot amid a largely modest recent profile at a mark of 52.

runners_data.name: Peig Sayers
runners_data.note: Runs for Miss McLoughlin who has a recent winner; a genuine hold-up horse whose recent form on 8f good ground shows finishes of 8th-22nd — the fade flag is consistent and the amateur jockey partnership does not improve the outlook in a competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Peig Sayers at least has experience over today's trip and going to call upon, and our rating of 55 suggests she holds more ability than her official mark of 44 implies, though consistent form has been hard to come by.

runners_data.name: Winston's Promise
runners_data.note: Liam Cusack's three-year-old has posted three consecutive eighth-place finishes and wears a hood; a true hold-up type forced to run closer than comfortable in this field, and the unbroken run of eighth-place efforts makes it hard to construct a winning case.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Winston's Promise faces a stiff task here; consecutive eighths offer little encouragement, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp 17-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Jazz Dreamers
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old for Seamus Fahey who has been absent recently; career record at 8f on good ground is unimpressive and the fade flag has been consistent — even if he gets a decent position, the form profile does not suggest a winning effort here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Jazz Dreamers has little to recommend him despite the experience of having run over today's trip and going, and 20 days between runs leaves him with no excuses on freshness.

runners_data.name: Lorr's Girl
runners_data.note: Rodger Sweeney has had no runners in 14 days and the horse has a modest record over 7-8f on good going; the 7lb claimer Pietropaolo rides and the tendency to hold up deep puts the horse at a disadvantage in a field this size — no strong angle to promote.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of unplaced efforts and an official rating of 40, Lorr's Girl is hard to fancy on these figures, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a manageable 23-day break carrying 123 lb from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Mullacash Buzz
runners_data.note: Thomas Dowling's eight-year-old has shown a habit of placing (three placed efforts in last five on good ground at 8f) without winning and comes in off 23 days; Rory Mulligan's 5lb claim is useful and if the race develops into a strong pace Mullacash Buzz has some late-race credibility among the hold-up types.
runners_data.comment: Mullacash Buzz has placed in each of his last two starts and, having run over today's trip and going before, arrives with some relevant experience behind him; yet he remains yet to win in recent starts and his draw at stall 16 is a neutral factor with 123 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Leannespour
runners_data.note: The three-year-old for Edward Lynam has a 4th on good ground over 7f as her best effort and the fade flag is noted; Declan McDonogh is a quality booking but the horse has unproven stamina for a flat mile and the form is light.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, Leannespour faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a handy 20-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Starflow
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead has been exceptionally active (4/34 in 14 days) and this three-year-old returns after 74 days off — the gap is the main concern, and while the horse handles good ground, the form at 8f is modest and the tongue-tie plus absence make this a watch-and-see profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 14th of 19 on our figures, Starflow has been consistently well held of late, and 74 days off the track adds to the concerns; the experience over today's trip is some comfort, but he has plenty to prove from stall 17 carrying 121 lb.

runners_data.name: Reponse Finale
runners_data.note: No listed jockey in the data is notable; Gavin Cromwell is active and the mare won over 10f on good ground earlier in her form string, suggesting she stays well — ran only two days ago which is a significant durability question, but the form contains a win and two places on similar ground making her one of the more interesting of the redistributed group.
runners_data.comment: Reponse Finale won last time out but returns just two days later carrying 132 lb from stall nine, which tests her stamina for a quick back-up; she has run over today's trip and going before, though her recent form is patchy beyond that latest success.

races.paceDynamic: Launch Time is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, with only Borora Aura likely to push forward alongside, faces no meaningful pace pressure — expect a controlled, even gallop on good ground over a flat mile at Cork. With the pace scenario unlikely to become truly searching, the race will likely be run at a tempo that suits those racing close to the action rather than those needing a strong pace to reel back the leaders from off it. The bulk of this field are genuine hold-up or midfield horses, but the redistribution is significant: James Henry, Thompson Gunner, Morning Approach, Peig Sayers, Winston's Promise, Jazz Dreamers, Lorr's Girl, Mullacash Buzz, Leannespour, Starflow, and Reponse Finale are all true hold-up types squeezed into a midfield representation that flatters their ability to get competitive positions. The tactical verdict is clear: with a single uncontested pace-setter and a field full of closers who cannot all find their ideal racing room, prominent-to-midfield horses who track the controlled pace and respond in the straight hold the structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Launch Time Dictates Controlled Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Launch Time leads at a sustainable tempo and the field cannot muster enough pressure to lift the pace genuinely.
scenarios.body: Launch Time, comfortable on good ground with Colin Keane riding and recent course-and-distance form, controls every yard and has enough in reserve to repel challengers at the business end; Borora Aura, next best placed, tracks and benefits from the honest but not punishing pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Picks Off Leader
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or early-midfield horse tracks the controlled pace and produces a sustained run that overtakes the front pair inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop gifts an energy advantage to the horse just off the pace who avoids traffic trouble; Glamazon and Dawn Flame, both capable of racing handily, are positioned to attack the leader without needing the race to be run at a punishing tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Mow Down Modest Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just slow enough that the final-furlong sprint becomes genuinely contested and a true hold-up runner finds a gap in time.
scenarios.body: Imnotleavinyou and Mullacash Buzz carry the best claims among the authentic hold-up types and have shown the ability to finish late on good ground at similar trips; however, most runners competing for this shape are redistributed types not naturally suited to the rear, reducing the overall probability of a clean late sweep.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the field races in a tight group throughout and a sprint develops in the straight, causing chaos and opening the door for a random finisher.
scenarios.body: A cavalry charge finish with 19 runners on flat good ground risks pockets and traffic, making a winner from deep in the pack plausible at long odds; Reponse Finale, with a course win on good ground and a strong finishing effort on her best form, is best-placed to capitalise if daylight appears late.

watchPoints.text: Launch Time (Colin Keane) is the only natural front-runner in a 19-runner field — if she gets a clean lead at a controlled pace, she may simply never be headed and the race is over as a betting contest early in the straight.

Thompson Gunner ran just two days ago and is now asked to race significantly closer to the pace than his natural position — monitor in the betting for any confidence, but the short turnaround combined with the positional mismatch makes him a significant risk at any price.

Reponse Finale also ran two days ago; if she lines up, watch whether the yard (Cromwell) has targeted this race specifically, as back-to-back runs in handicaps can indicate confidence — but the distance drop from 10f to 8f may blunt her stamina advantage.

With 11 of 19 runners redistributed from their natural hold-up positions into midfield on the map, the draw and early positioning will be critical — horses that can find a prominent pitch without burning energy will have a structural edge over true closers trapped wide or deep.

Glamazon (Shane Foley / Mrs Harrington) — the trainer-jockey combination has placed twice in 28 recent runners and the filly's course record on good ground over 8f makes her one of the horses most worth tracking through the early stages to assess whether she secures a racing position that suits.
